predecessors.name: Dvaravati
predecessors.text: Haripuñjaya (Lamphun), the Mon city-state of the Dvaravati world

successors.name: Lan Na Kingdom
successors.text: the Ping valley round Lamphun and Lampang: 'Mangrai incorporated the kingdom into Lan Na'

ledger.x: c. 750: Haripunjaya arises at Lamphun. 'The actual beginning is placed at around 750 AD'; infobox 'More probable founding of Haripunjaya: 750' and 'Legendary founding of Haripunjaya by Suthep: 629'; the chronicles say four hermits founded it 'between 629-57 AD' and Camadevi, daughter of the Lavo king, was its first…

c. 750: the rest of the realm. Page silent on dates: the legends have Jamadevi's twin ruling Lampang and Jamadevi defeating 'Khun Luang Wilangka' (the Lan Na version has him 'withdrawing to the hills') at Raming Nakhon (Chiang Mai). The Cliopatria outline is taken as the realm from the founding.
ledger.cp: Lawa chiefdoms of Raming Nakhon (Khun Luang Wilangka)

ledger.x: 927: the war ends as Tambralinga takes Lavo.
927: a Lavo king takes the Haripunjaya throne.
1188: the southern Haripunjaya lands pass to Angkor.

wars.name: Lavo-Haripunjaya war (925-927)
wars.outcome: 'Battles between Lavo and Haripunjaya are recorded from 925 to 927'; no border change on the pages.

wars.name: Haripunjaya's annexation of Lavo (1052)
wars.outcome: Adityaraja 'annexed Lavo in 1052 and appointed his brother, Chadachota, the king of Lavo'.

wars.name: Conflict with the Khmers over Lavo (from 1002)
wars.outcome: 'The Khmers took over Lavo from Tambralinga in 1002, and Haripunjaya came into conflict with them'; the page gives no further date or border change.

wars.name: Invasions from Umongasela (10th-11th centuries)
wars.outcome: 'Invasions from Umongasela were unsuccessful during the 10th-11th centuries'; no border moved.

wars.name: Mangrai's conquest of Hariphunchai (1291-1292)
wars.outcome: 'In 1292 the city was besieged and captured by Mangrai' after his merchant Ai Fa had undermined King Yi Ba as chief minister; Yi Ba fled to Lampang; Mangrai made it part of Lan Na.

certainty.note: A Mon mandala known from chronicles and inscriptions; no page opened gives a boundary, so every frontier (Lavo, the Khmer lands, the Shan hills, Pagan's cis-Salween claims) is approximate.
